Most games really.

Not saying that to sound hardcore or anything, but there isn't a lot of challenge to be found in the majority of video games. They aren't really designed to be hard outside of specific titles. Especially modern games.

For every Dark Souls or Bayonetta, there's a hundred games that don't penalize death or have auto regenerating health. Every Gran Tourismo has a dozen Need for Speed arcade type games.

There are hard games out there, but generally you have to actively seek them out. Hard does not necessarily equate to fun all the time either. Part of the appeal of Saint's Row is the fact that you're absurdly powerful and just in it for the lulz. Games are a storytelling medium these days, and are often far more about the spectacle than the challenge.

Games aren't designed to eat quarters anymore. "Nintendo hard" games were from a different market with different design goals that gradually shifted into a more story driven medium. Players are intended to be able to finish games and progress a story, not drop quarters into a slot to cycle through levels for a high score.

For the most part games these days are designed to have enough resistance that a player feels like they're working through it, but not so much that a casual player will get discouraged and quit. As a result, most games are meant to be time consuming, but not difficult.

The other end of that is multiplayer focused titles. Where the 'game' part of it is really just an introduction to the mechanics you'll be using in online matches. Again, they aren't really designed to be challenging, but rather to teach and reinforce the basic skills players need to compete in matches.

That doesn't mean they can't have a good story or anything, just that he focus isn't on challenging the player with difficult to overcome obstacles. It's still meant to entertain, but also to learn how things work in a gradual manner for later use against other players.
